correctness.rationale: All feasible local selections are partitioned by parent/self-selection and self-domination into four exhaustive state cases. The min-plus two-state OR aggregator exactly imposes at least one selected child and is associative; two tree traversals cover all directed edges in O(n). Full constrained minima follow by excluding an external parent. The independent brute enumerator checked 18,729 tree inputs up to 13 vertices (exhaustive labelled through 7) and the predicted subdivision property on all 1,441 trees through 6 vertices. The infinite theorem is supported by structural induction, not numerical extrapolation. The subdivision criterion is explicitly a previously proved Theorem 3.2, used with correct nonstar hypothesis.

originality.rationale: The June 2026 primary explicitly leaves formal linear-time computation of N_iota(T) to future work and states the existing quadratic bound. The 2025 all/some/no membership algorithm is for ordinary domination, not isolating sets. The 2026 broader vertex-edge domination algorithm computes an optimum, not per-vertex constrained optima, and the distinct February 2026 subdivision-critical tree result uses the universal quantifier. Semantic database searches did not surface direct prior coverage, with residual risks explicitly recorded.
residual_risks: The main 2026 source explicitly predicts the linear-time rerooting solution and characterizes it as technical, so the conceptual novelty is limited to a fully specified and proved recurrence and constructive classification.
The cited 2025 isolation-optimization paper was not read in full; its details could include a comparable two-pass optimal-status routine.
A relevant 2025 PDF was read for introduction and algorithmic statement but visual screenshot retrieval failed after redirect, and later pages were not scrutinized.
Unindexed unpublished implementations, general weighted-tree constraint-satisfaction algorithms or equivalent presentations may cover the recurrence.

value.rationale: An explicitly requested algorithmic gap is closed: linear time, optimal for reading the tree input, replaces the quadratic characterization-based check while simultaneously returning the complete all/some/none optimum-membership classification and all constrained optimum costs. This is a substantive sharp-complexity and structural-output result on arbitrary trees. The generic rerooting concept is known and anticipated, but the concrete isolating-set boundary states and rigorous closure of the open algorithmic task are useful; this is not a numerical tweak or arbitrary finite slice.
